top_story: As UN funding cuts remove food aid from roughly half a million people in Gaza, families already displaced by war face soaring prices and the renewed prospect of famine, deepening a humanitarian collapse that extends beyond battlefield dynamics. The following day, oil climbed above $115 a barrel as fears of renewed US strikes on Iran and threatened retaliation against Gulf infrastructure pulled the crisis into a wider regional and economic frame. The immediate picture is of a conflict system in which pressure on civilians in Gaza and Palestinians in Israeli custody is unfolding alongside escalation risks that could rapidly raise costs and insecurity across the Middle East.
